story: Administrative Order 359, Alaska's standing order directing every executive agency to use AI to review state spending, passes to Governor-elect Kreiss-Tomkins and his new OMB director

repeat_reasons: AO 359 page, first response summarized rather than quoted
source_fetch_summary.showrunner_fetches: AO 359 page (curl), ADN November 19th (curl), omb.alaska.gov (503 twice)

claims.claim: Governor Mike Dunleavy signed Administrative Order 359 on August 4th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: DATED this 4th day of August 2025.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Background; the order remains in force.

claims.claim: AO 359 orders a statewide annual Government Efficiency Review of all executive branch agencies.
claims.verbatim: a statewide annual Government Efficiency Review of all executive branch agencies
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 directs every agency to use technology and artificial intelligence to review large datasets to determine how State of Alaska funds are actually being spent.
claims.verbatim: Utilize technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to review large datasets in order to determine how State of Alaska funds are actually being spent.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Full clause confirmed by showrunner's own fetch of the order (out/2026-11-22/src/ao359.html); the fact-checker's live fetch returned the first half verbatim.

claims.claim: AO 359 directs agencies to recommend where technological or AI resources can realize efficiencies and better outcomes.
claims.verbatim: Recommend where technological or AI resources can realize efficiencies and better outcomes.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 requires OMB to annually publish a list of funds granted by agency, to what entities and for what purposes.
claims.verbatim: OMB shall annually publish a list of funds granted, by agency, to what entities, and for what purposes.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Duty only. Whether OMB published such a list is UNVERIFIED (omb.alaska.gov 503). Never claim either way.

claims.claim: The AO 359 agency participation list contains seven duties.
claims.verbatim: Identify target areas and practices to review. Utilize technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to review large datasets ... Review and publish how funds granted to non-state entities are being spent. Recommend a targeted level of reductions ... Recommend state processes to be updated or modernized. Recommend where technological or AI resources can realize efficiencies and better outcomes. Recommend services that can be contracted out.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Count read off the list by both fact-checker and showrunner.

claims.claim: AO 359 sets out six objectives for the Government Efficiency Review.
claims.verbatim: Identify potential savings. Improve efficiency of operations. Modernize processes to fully integrate IT solutions. Recommend services to be contracted out. Simplify operations. Focus the state's limited workforce where most needed.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Six review objectives; distinct from the seven-item Goals list.

claims.claim: AO 359 names grants to non-State of Alaska entities as an initial focus area.
claims.value: Grants to non-State of Alaska entities
claims.verbatim: Grants to non-State of Alaska entities.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 names accounts payable as an initial focus area.
claims.verbatim: Accounts Payable.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 applies to executive branch agencies including departments, boards, commissions and public corporations.
claims.verbatim: including departments, boards, commissions, and public corporations
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 says the state's savings accounts hold only enough reserves to fund seven months of government operations.
claims.verbatim: The State of Alaska's savings accounts now hold only enough reserves to fund seven months of government operations.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: The administration's own August 2025 framing. Attribute to the order.

claims.claim: AO 359 took effect immediately and remains in effect until revoked.
claims.verbatim: This Administrative Order takes effect immediately and remains in effect until revoked.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Whether Kreiss-Tomkins will keep or revoke it is not reported anywhere fetched.

claims.claim: The governor's office announced on August 4th, 2025 that Dunleavy issued two administrative orders on government efficiency and regulatory reform.
claims.verbatim: Governor Dunleavy Issues Two Administrative Orders to Improve Government Efficiency and Regulatory Reform
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: Dunleavy said the order ensures the state prioritizes critical needs, eliminates waste and safeguards its financial stability.
claims.verbatim: This order ensures we prioritize critical needs, eliminate waste, and safeguard the state's financial stability.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: Alaska's News Source reported in 2025 that agencies would be required to use technology and artificial intelligence to improve transparency and accountability.
claims.verbatim: Agencies will also be required to use technology and artificial intelligence to improve transparency and accountability
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Wil Courtney)

claims.claim: The Petersburg Pilot reported that Dunleavy directed departments to use artificial intelligence software to help identify budget cuts.
claims.verbatim: artificial intelligence software
claims.source_outlet: Petersburg Pilot (James Brooks)

claims.claim: Governor's spokesperson Grant Robinson said the review may result in eliminating grants to non-State of Alaska entities in some areas of the budget.
claims.verbatim: In some areas of the budget, this may result in eliminating grants to non-State of Alaska entities,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Wil Courtney)

claims.claim: State Sen. Bill Wielechowski said finding efficiencies is what the governor was supposed to have been doing for the last seven years.
claims.verbatim: I hope that he's able to find efficiencies, but this is what he's supposed to have been doing for the last seven years.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Wil Courtney)

claims.claim: The Juneau Independent reported that AO 359 resembles DOGE-style mandates adopted in at least 26 states.
claims.verbatim: Administrative Order No. 359:
claims.source_outlet: Juneau Independent (Mark Sabbatini)
claims.notes: Paraphrase only; do not use on a slide.

claims.claim: Governor-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins named Alexei Painter to lead the Office of Management and Budget.
claims.verbatim: Painter will lead Kreiss-Tomkins' Office of Management and Budget, overseeing the governor's budget.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)

claims.claim: Painter previously worked as an OMB analyst and as an economist in the Department of Revenue.
claims.verbatim: He previously worked as an OMB analyst and an economist in the Department of Revenue.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)

claims.claim: To take the job Painter is leaving his role with the Legislature, where he helped guide lawmakers' budget process.
claims.verbatim: To take the job, Painter is leaving his role with the Legislature, where he helped guide lawmakers' budget process in recent years.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)
claims.notes: Verbatim confirmed by showrunner fetch (out/2026-11-22/src/adn.html). No exact title; do not print a title.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins is set to take office on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: prepares to take office on Dec. 7.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)

claims.claim: The Kreiss-Tomkins transition team received more than 300 resumes and over 400 ideas.
claims.verbatim: the transition team received more than 300 resumes and over 400 ideas.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)
claims.notes: ADN does not mention AI or AO 359; linking Painter to AO 359 is the deck's framing via C38.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission approved Mayor Grier Hopkins' proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers.
claims.verbatim: approved Mayor Grier Hopkins' proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)
claims.notes: Approval date conflicting in source; do not state it.

claims.claim: The planning commission extended the proposed data center moratorium from 12 months to 18 months.
claims.verbatim: That's when the clock will start for the 18-month moratorium.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)

claims.claim: The commission extended the borough administration's deadline for research and recommendations from six months to 10 months.
claims.verbatim: (paraphrase)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)

claims.claim: Hopkins said the assembly vote will likely happen on January 14th and that is when the moratorium clock would start.
claims.verbatim: That's when the clock will start for the 18-month moratorium.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)

claims.claim: Hopkins said a data center on Eielson Air Force Base built purely for a government purpose would likely not be subject to the borough moratorium.
claims.verbatim: If it comes in as purely for a government purpose, I believe that would be not subject to our moratorium.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)

claims.claim: Hopkins said the borough is working to turn the Eielson gray area black and white.
claims.verbatim: turn that gray area black and white.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)

claims.claim: Mat-Su Borough officials sent a letter asking the state to reconsider transferring about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: about 6,800 acres of land near Houston
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)

claims.claim: The borough letter says Point MacKenzie and portions of West Susitna offer more appropriate locations for these uses.
claims.verbatim: The Borough believes that Point Mackenzie and portions of West Susitna offer more appropriate locations for these uses.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)

claims.claim: The letter cites 180 million dollars already spent on a rail bed near Point MacKenzie.
claims.verbatim: (paraphrase)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)

claims.claim: People who commented during the proposal process can request reconsideration by November 30th.
claims.verbatim: Nov. 30
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)

claims.claim: Borough Manager Mike Brown and Mayor Edna DeVries signed the letter.
claims.verbatim: (paraphrase)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)

claims.claim: AO 359 makes the Office of Management and Budget responsible for implementing the order.
claims.verbatim: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) shall be responsible for the implementation of this Administrative Order.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 tells OMB to annually lead an executive branch-wide review of base budget expenditures and practices.
claims.verbatim: OMB shall annually lead an executive branch-wide Government Efficiency Review of base budget expenditures and practices
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: On Wednesday November 18th Kreiss-Tomkins announced three first picks, Ira Slomski-Pritz as chief of staff, Alexei Painter as OMB director and Becky Windt Pearson as AIDEA adviser.
claims.verbatim: selected Ira Slomski-Pritz as his chief of staff; Alexei Painter as director of the Office of Management and Budget; and Becky Windt Pearson as adviser on the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)
claims.notes: 'on Wednesday announced' in a November 19th piece; Wednesday was November 18th.

claims.claim: AO 359 says the state has no process in place to review zero base budget appropriations and expenditures.
claims.verbatim: There is currently, however, no process in place to review zero base budget appropriations and expenditures.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 tells every agency to review and publish how funds granted to non-state entities are being spent.
claims.verbatim: Review and publish how funds granted to non-state entities are being spent.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: Two of the seven AO 359 agency duties name AI.
claims.verbatim: Utilize technology and artificial intelligence (AI) ... Recommend where technological or AI resources can realize efficiencies and better outcomes.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska
claims.notes: Count of duties naming AI, read off the list.

claims.claim: AO 359 tells agencies to recommend a targeted level of reductions through savings on wasteful and unnecessary spending.
claims.verbatim: Recommend a targeted level of reductions through savings on wasteful and unnecessary spending.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 cites OPEC's December 2024 decision to increase output as a cause of falling oil revenues.
claims.verbatim: oil revenues are falling due to global events such as OPEC's December 2024 decision to increase output.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: AO 359 tells OMB the review should modernize processes to fully integrate IT solutions.
claims.verbatim: Modernize processes to fully integrate IT solutions.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Governor, State of Alaska

claims.claim: Becky Windt Pearson will have a leading role in the incoming administration's review of AIDEA's operations, governance and strategic direction.
claims.verbatim: a leading role in the incoming administration's review of (AIDEA's) operations, governance, and strategic direction.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)
